content: Diabetic retinopathy is a significant ocular complication that occurs in individuals with both type 1 and type 2 diabetes. The likelihood of developing this condition is closely associated with the duration of diabetes and the degree of glycemic control achieved. It is one of the primary causes of vision loss in adults between the ages of 20 and 74 years. Maintaining effective glycemic control has been shown to reduce both the onset and progression of diabetic retinopathy. This, in turn, decreases the need for surgical interventions and helps preserve visual function.
